power: Configure power management for block devices Add udev rule that runs a script to configure APM for block devices when supported, and the standby timeout otherwise. APM level 254 (max performance) is used when running on AC, and level 1 (lowest power) when on battery. The standby timeout is 2h on AC and 5s on battery. For SanDisk SSDs power management is not configured since the implementation is too aggressive (b/35524329). BUG=chromium:741938, chromium:214886 TEST=butterfly (w/ HDD) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 1 plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 254 peppy (KINGSTON SNS4151) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 1 plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 254 falco (LITEONIT LSS-16, APM not supported) hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = not supported unplug AC # wait 30s dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: standby (most of the times) repeat 10x plug AC # wait 5s dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: active/idle repeat 10x wolf (SanDisk SSD i110) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = off dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: standby (most of the times) repeat 10x plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = off dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: active/idle repeat 10x CQ-DEPEND=CL:915302 Change-Id: Iaa3939f12640116ed4d5c06a25c8c0ee0a47eeae Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/914537 Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

Update Harfbuzz to 1.7.5 and up to 0bff6991 This is to match Harfbuzz on other platforms. harfbuzz-1.7.5.324.tar.bz2 was obtained as following from the harfbuzz git tree : 1. git checkout 0bff6991 2. sh autogen.sh 3. ./configure 4. make distcheck 5. rename the top directory to harfbuzz-1.7.5.324 6. make a tar ball. Making a giant patch against harfbuzz-1.7.5.tar.bz to go up to 0bff6991 (324 CLs) does not work because applying the patch changes Makefile.am (multiple of them) and configure.ac. With the time stamp of those files updated by the patch application, `make' looks for the same version of aclocal and autoconf as used in 'make distcheck' step above eventually leading to a build failure. The simplest way is to upload the tar ball made above to the CrOS common storage and use it directly without a patch. sys-apps/lvm2: udev_get_udevdir to get_udevdir udev_get_udevdir has been deprecated for a while. crrev.com/c/941974 will change it to an error, so switch to the new function. Since this is portage-stable, this should ideally be an upgrade to the newer version instead. However, there have been 148 lvm2 releases since we last updated and the current upstream stable version of lvm2 corrupts the stateful partition when the system boots. Patch out the deprecated function here as a temporary measure to unblock updates depending on this while I debug what's wrong with the newer lvm2 versions. core: add chip-specific memory regions definition mechanism When a chip has special/non-contiguous SRAM physical memory region, rather than extending the generic linker file ad nauseam, define a mechanism to declare a chip specific list of those regions. To do so, a chip must declare the CONFIG_CHIP_MEMORY_REGIONS configuration and have a memory_regions.inc with the list of regions. The special-purpose preprocessed chip/<chip_name>/memory_regions.inc file has one region declaration per line using the following macro: REGION(name, attributes, start_address, size) Each region will get a proper MEMORY entry and a section in the linker file. the __SECTION(region_name) helper is provided as a convenience to declare variable in a specific region. Note: those 'special' regions are NOT cleared at startup contrary to .bss. Signed-off-by: Vincent Palatin <vpalatin@chromium.org> BRANCH=none BUG=b:67081508 TEST=on ZerbleBarn, along with the following CLs, run the firmware with large arrays in special AHB memory regions.
